value.rationale: Angular-gap majorization and exact affine invariants of rotated regular polygon intersections are canonical mathematical objects. The complete strict two-copy order and an all-n three-copy obstruction pin down the first transition in the number of rotations at which expected Schur-convexity can fail, in pointed contrast with the previously proved Schur-concavity of the Mahler product on the identical family. The negative cubic term is structurally nontrivial: first- and second-order variations cancel on the compared pair. This is not a new label for an existing invariant or an arbitrary selected polygon.
